record.paper_title: Some open problems in control theory.
record.context_brief: blowup avoidance for nonlinear heat equation
record.original_question: For a one-dimensional heat equation with a cubic nonlinearity, can the blowup phenomenon be avoided by a suitable control strategy?

evidence.quote: 6)7) For a one-dimensional heat equation with cubic nonlinearity, can the blowup phenomenon be avoided? Is the equation small time controllable?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the one-dimensional semilinear heat equation with cubic nonlinearity on the bounded interval (0,1):

  y_t(t,x) - y_{xx}(t,x) = y(t,x)^3 + 1_{\omega}(x) u(t,x), \quad (t,x) \in (0,T)\times(0,1),
  y(t,0) = y(t,1) = 0, \quad t \in (0,T),
  y(0,x) = y_0(x), \quad x \in (0,1),

where \omega \subset (0,1) is a fixed nonempty open subinterval (the control region), 1_{\omega} is its indicator function, and u \in L^2((0,T)\times(0,1)) is an internal control supported in \omega. It is known that, in the absence of control (u \equiv 0), there exist smooth initial data y_0 for which the solution y blows up in finite time, i.e., \lim_{t \to T^*} \|y(t,\cdot)\|_{L^\infty(0,1)} = +\infty for some T^* < +\infty.

Question: For every initial datum y_0 (say in H^1_0(0,1) or smoother) and every T>0, does there exist a control u \in L^2((0,T)\times \omega) such that the corresponding solution y of the controlled equation exists globally on [0,T] (i.e., the blowup phenomenon is avoided)?

Equivalently: can the blowup of solutions of the cubic semilinear heat equation in one space dimension always be prevented by a suitable internal control localized on \omega?
artifact.status_search_result: Search results indicate active research on controllability and blowup of semilinear heat equations, including feedback controllability of blowup points and prevention-of-blowup results in related settings, but no source clearly resolves the specific question of whether internal controls can prevent blowup for the one-dimensional cubic semilinear heat equation. The status appears to remain open or at least not definitively settled in the literature surveyed.

status_evidence.title: Feedback controllability for blowup points of heat equation
status_evidence.snippet: Feedback control results addressing whether one can drive solutions to blow up at prescribed points; the converse problem of preventing blowup is discussed as distinct.
status_evidence.claim: Related control problems for blowup of heat equations are studied, but distinct from blowup avoidance.

status_evidence.title: Prevention of blowup via Neumann heat kernel
status_evidence.snippet: Studies conditions under which blowup can be prevented in nonlinear heat equations.
status_evidence.claim: Recent (2025) work on blowup prevention indicates the topic remains active.

status_evidence.title: Feedback approximate controllability of blowup points for the heat equation
status_evidence.snippet: 2025 preprint on feedback control for blowup points; open cases remain.
status_evidence.claim: Indicates the broader controllability-of-blowup question still has open subcases.
